book.title: Ibn Jubayr: A Great Traveler from Al-Andalus (A1)

pages.title: Al-Andalus
pages.content:
From 711 to 1492, Muslims ruled parts of Spain and Portugal. This place had a name: Al-Andalus. Muslims, Christians and Jews lived there together. They worked, bought, sold and studied together.

Al-Andalus had big, beautiful cities. Córdoba was the biggest city in Western Europe. Sevilla had 1,000 mosques. People there were good at art, medicine and science.

Ibn Jubayr was born in Valencia in 1145. Valencia is a city in the east of Spain, near the sea. Ibn Jubayr was a famous traveler.

pages.title: A Big Dream
pages.content:
When he was young, Ibn Jubayr studied a lot. He learned about Islam, languages and books. Then he worked in Granada. He was a secretary for the governor.

He had a big dream. He wanted to go on Hajj. He also wanted to learn new things and see other Muslim countries.

He started his long journey in 1183. He took a diary with him. He wrote in it every day. People call his book the Rihla. Rihla means “travel book”. In those days, travel was very hard and dangerous. His journey was more than two years long.

pages.title: A Storm at Sea
pages.content:
In February 1183, Ibn Jubayr left Granada. He went to Ceuta in North Africa. There, he got on a ship. The ship went past Sardinia and Sicily. Then a very bad storm came. The people on the ship were afraid. But the ship was fine.

In March, the ship came to Alexandria, in Egypt. There, Ibn Jubayr saw the famous lighthouse of Alexandria. It was very tall and very old. He loved it.

After eight days, he went to Cairo.

pages.title: Cairo and Saladin
pages.content:
In Cairo, the leader was Sultan Saladin. Ibn Jubayr liked him very much. Saladin was kind and fair. He helped mosques, schools and hospitals. The roads were safe day and night.

Ibn Jubayr visited a big hospital. It was free for everyone. It had different rooms for men and for women. He saw the pyramids, too.

Saladin built houses for students, teachers and poor people. Every day, he gave 2,000 loaves of bread to poor people.

pages.title: Eight Months in Mecca
pages.content:
From Egypt, Ibn Jubayr traveled to the Red Sea with a caravan of camels. Some people had very big and beautiful tents!

In August 1183, he arrived in Mecca. He stayed there for more than eight months. He made the Hajj. He visited the Ka’ba with great love and respect. People came to Mecca from Persia, India and Africa.

Mecca is in a narrow valley. But there is room for very big groups of people. Ibn Jubayr said, “This is one of Allah’s miracles.”

vocabulary.definition: A group of people and animals on a journey.
A small house made of cloth.
A feeling that someone is important.

pages.title: Baghdad and Damascus
pages.content:
In April 1184, Ibn Jubayr went to Medina. Then he traveled through the desert to Baghdad. Baghdad was the capital of the Abbasids. It had 2,000 public baths!

Next, he went to Aleppo and Damascus. He visited the Great Mosque of Damascus. He wrote about its tall minarets, its beautiful mosaics and its water clock.

In Damascus, students and travelers from other countries stayed in madrasas for free. Ibn Jubayr liked this very much.

pages.title: A Ship Hits the Rocks
pages.content:
Then Ibn Jubayr went to Acre, in Palestine. At that time, the Crusaders ruled Palestine. He waited two weeks for good winds. Then he got on a ship for home.

The sea was very dangerous. There were big storms. Near Sicily, the ship hit some rocks and broke. Ibn Jubayr almost died, but he was safe in the end. The king of Sicily, William II, helped the people from the ship.

In 1185, Ibn Jubayr arrived home. He thanked Allah. He always prayed in danger.

vocabulary.definition: Soldiers from Europe who came to fight.
A very big stone.

pages.title: Travel and Knowledge
pages.content:
Travel in those days was dangerous. At sea, there were storms. In the desert, there were thieves. They took everything from travelers. Caravans traveled at night, because the sun was too hot in the day.

At home in Granada, Ibn Jubayr wrote his travel book. He taught hadiths. Hadiths are the words and actions of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). Later, he went to Mecca again. He died in Alexandria in 1217.

His journeys gave him a lot of knowledge. He told young people, “Travel and learn.”

pages.title: Language Review
pages.content: Review the language from all chapters.

exercises.title: Look: Two Kinds of Past
exercises.instructions: Put each verb in the right group.
exercises.question: How does each verb show the past?
exercises.explanation: Many verbs add -ed: study → studied, visit → visited. Some verbs change: write → wrote, see → saw, go → went, take → took.

feedback.correct: Well done. You found the two kinds of past.
feedback.incorrect: Say the verb today: study, write … Does it add -ed or change?

exercises.title: Practise: In, On, At
exercises.question: Which word goes with the time?
exercises.explanation: In + year or month: in 1183, in March. At night.

feedback.incorrect: In 1183. At night.

exercises.title: Practise: There Was, There Were
exercises.instructions: Choose there was or there were.
exercises.question: One or many?

formChoices.sentence: At sea, [choice] a very bad storm.

exercises.explanation: One thing: there was. Two or more: there were.

feedback.incorrect: Thieves = many. A storm = one.

exercises.title: Practise: The Biggest and More Than
exercises.instructions: Fill the gaps with the words.
exercises.question: How big? How long?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Córdoba was the [blank] city in Western Europe. His journey was [blank] than two years long. He stayed in Mecca for more [blank] eight months.
exercises.explanation: The biggest = number one. More than = over.

feedback.incorrect: Find these words in Chapters 1, 2 and 5.

exercises.title: Practise: Fix One Word
exercises.instructions: Find the wrong word. Write the right word.
exercises.question: Which word is wrong?

errorItems.sentence: Ibn Jubayr writed a travel book.
He goed to Medina in April.

exercises.explanation: “Write” and “go” change in the past: wrote, went.

feedback.incorrect: Write → wrote. Go → went. They do not take -ed.

exercises.title: Use: My Trip
exercises.instructions: Write three sentences about a trip.
exercises.question: Where did you go?
exercises.explanation: Use in, one past verb and for + time.

discussionPrompts.question: One “in + year or month”: “In July, I …”
discussionPrompts.example: In July, I went to Antalya.

discussionPrompts.question: One past verb: “I saw …”
discussionPrompts.example: I saw the sea.

discussionPrompts.question: One “for + time”: “I stayed there for …”
discussionPrompts.example: I stayed there for five days.

exercises.title: The Journey of Ibn Jubayr
exercises.question: What happened first?

sequencingItems.text: Ibn Jubayr made the Hajj in Mecca.
Ibn Jubayr visited the Great Mosque of Damascus.
The ship hit some rocks near Sicily.

exercises.explanation: The storm (Chapter 3) → Mecca (Chapter 5) → Damascus (Chapter 6) → Sicily (Chapter 7).

feedback.correct: Great! You know the journey of Ibn Jubayr.
feedback.incorrect: Think about the order of the chapters.
